findings.title: Hope as Expectant Nearness
findings.claim: As an exploratory analogy, hope for mercy can be heard as expectancy approaching its threshold, while retaining its ordinary anticipatory sense.
findings.mechanism: Yarjūna carries the focus's ordinary hope; the nearby birth-nearing branch meets the womb image attributed to raḥmatahu and the comparative nearness of aqrabu, letting hoped-for mercy feel imminent without changing the subject or object of hope.
findings.reader_payoff: Hope may feel not only as looking toward a future good but as the approach of a threshold where mercy is near.
findings.containment: This does not identify the hopeful subjects as pregnant, claim literal birth, change the meaning of yarjūna, or establish etymology; ordinary hope remains.

findings.title: The Invoked Figure as a Sign That Draws Onward
findings.claim: As an exploratory analogy, an invoked figure can function as a retained sign that draws the seeker onward toward the Lord, rather than as a reservoir dispensing access.
findings.mechanism: The focus's calling verb carries the attributed retained-residue image; the immediate active seeking verb supplies onward movement, and al-wasīla with aqrabu points that movement toward nearness to God. This changes the before-reading of the invoked figure as a source of access into a pointer within the seeker's route.
findings.reader_payoff: Invocation can be perceived as redirecting attention and approach instead of guaranteeing access through the invoked figure.
findings.containment: Calling, seeking, and nearness retain their ordinary focus meanings. The milk-residue image is analogical, never an asserted etymology or a literal scene in the ayah.

epistemic.reason: The HFT word coordinates and roots return to supplied QAC carriers, while the branch role remains legacy_unbound, analogical, and explicitly exploratory.
